To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we show how to decouple the behavior policy and proximal policy in policy optimization, and that doing so makes the policy optimization algorithms batch size invariant.

(1) policy optimization algorithms are batch size-invariant, if they use a decoupled proximal policy and behavior policy; (2) the batch size-invariance is due to a new kind of policy correction term, called a policy gradient offset, which is the gradient of the policy objective with respect to the proximal policy; and (3) the batch size can be made arbitrarily large, while keeping the policy gradient offset small, by increasing the number of off-policy corrections.

(a) PPO can be made batch size-invariant by decoupling the proximal policy from the behavior policy, (b) PPO can make efficient use of stale (old) data by using the proximal policy for off-policy corrections, and (c) the batch size can be reduced by a factor of 10 with only a slight increase in the number of environment steps, while the number of parameters remains the same
